The do(a) notation triggers causal scrutiny, but no effect contrast, identification strategy, overlap analysis, or counterfactual validation is provided. title: DRIFT: Direct-Recursive Intervention-Conditioned Forecasting of ICU Physiological Trajectories

The authors explicitly disclaim causal effects and keep outcomes fixed during path replacement; causal fields are therefore NA, not positive evidence. Code is promised only upon publication.

title: Towards Causality-Aware Inferring: A Sequential Discriminative Approach for Medical Diagnosis.
evidence_anchors: Methods define MZ (586/142; 66 symptoms/4 diseases) and DX (423/104; 41 symptoms/5 diseases), propensity latent matching, progressive assurance inquiry/diagnosis, Ptrain-to-Pall OOD evaluation, 1/3-symptom inquiry budgets, five-fold analysis, and five seeds; Results include matching/masking ablations, sequential diagnostic success, OOD comparisons, and six-physician blinded evaluation; official CAMAD repository provides code.

title: Towards Surgical World-Action Modeling: A Preliminary Joint Visual-Trajectory Forecasting for Surgical Motion Planning
evidence_anchors: Secs. 1-2 pp. 2-6; Fig. 1 p. 4; Sec. 3 pp. 6-8 and Table 1 p. 8; Fig. 2 and conclusion pp. 8-9

It earns direct state/dynamics and free-running rollout evidence because decoded visual states and trajectory errors are reported across five segments of a fully autoregressive 15-step rollout. Decision evidence is only an offline planning proxy. The single benchmark, missing split details, no repeated-run statistics, absent uncertainty, and lack of public training code limit external and reproducibility evidence.
